description:
Check whether an answer you found in a source is bound to the question: is the quote copied verbatim from the document you cite, and is that passage about the entity and the conditions (time, place, version, unit) the question asks about, rather than about a neighbouring entity? Call it before you state an answer taken from a web page or document. Pass the documents you actually read, unchanged. The verdict is computed by deterministic string rules (no model, no network) when you pass 'constraints'.
Verdicts: ACCEPT - you may give the answer and cite the quote. RESEARCH - the quote exists, but the passage is not clearly about the asked entity or conditions (or another entity is closer to it); look for a better source, using research_request.query, and verify again. ABSTAIN - the quote is not in the cited document, is too short, or the evidence lacks what the question presupposes; do not give this answer: copy the quote exactly, or say you could not verify it.
Limits: the gate checks binding, not truth. An ACCEPT means the evidence is about the right thing, not that the source is correct or that the value was read correctly.

answer.description: The answer value you intend to give.

checks.description: Which checks to run (default: all five). Leaving one out is an ablation; they always run in the canonical order shown in the enum.

constraints.description: What acceptable evidence must be about. Pass this to run the gate fully deterministically, without calling any model. Same format as the output of decompose_question. Required on this server (no decomposer model is configured).

attribute.description: What is asked about the entity, e.g. 'maximum daily dose'. Used only in the research request.

entity.description: The entity the question asks about.

aliases.description: Other names that count as a mention of the same entity (brand names, abbreviations).

kind.description: Optional free-text type, e.g. 'drug'. Not used by the checks.

name.description: Its name as it would appear in a source, e.g. 'Lisinopril'.

presuppositions.description: What the question takes for granted. Every key term must appear in the evidence.

key_terms.description: Words whose presence in the evidence the premise check looks for.

qualifiers.description: Conditions the evidence must also mention near the quote (time, place, version, unit, other).

aliases.description: Other surface forms of the same condition.

text.description: The condition as it would appear in a source, e.g. '2023'.

documents.description: Every document you read for this answer, with its full text as you saw it. Other documents matter: their subjects are the competing entities. Ids must be unique. At most 200000 characters per text and 1000000 in total.

id.description: A short id you choose, e.g. 'doc1'.

parameters.description: Gate parameters. Omit to use the defaults, which are the PROPOSED values of the study's pre-registration (section 5.1; not yet frozen). Any value you set is echoed in the output.

competitor_tie.description: Whether a competing entity exactly as close to the quote as the question's entity blocks the answer ('fail') or not ('pass').

lead_max_tokens.description: Longest lead term (in tokens) that counts as the subject of a document when looking for competing entities.

lead_min_repeats.description: How often a lead term must occur in its document to count as a competing entity.

min_quote_tokens.description: Smallest number of whitespace-separated tokens a quote must have.

premise_scope.description: Where presupposition key terms are looked for: the whole cited document, or only the window around the quote.

window_tokens.description: Largest number of tokens allowed between the quote and a mention of the entity, a qualifier or a competing entity.

question.description: The question exactly as it was asked.

quote.description: One continuous passage copied verbatim from the cited document that supports the answer (at least min_quote_tokens words).

source_id.description: The id of the document the quote is copied from.

name: verify_answer
title: Verify that an answer's evidence is about the question

description: Turn a question into the constraints that verify_answer checks: the entity, the asked attribute, qualifiers and presuppositions. Uses a language model configured by the server operator, so it is not deterministic and its API cost is paid by the operator's key. Review the result and pass it to verify_answer as 'constraints'. If no decomposer is configured, this tool returns an error: write the constraints yourself and pass them to verify_answer. No decomposer is configured on this server: calling this tool returns an explanation only.

question.description: The question exactly as it was asked.

name: decompose_question
title: Decompose a question into constraints (uses a model)
